kanban-claude 0.4.0.dev3

Runs now survive network outages and silent hangs, and a paused board restarts itself. CI that never ran can no longer pass as green, and a PR can no longer skip the warden or lose its Closes line. Work in several cards lands as milestone branches. The Linux support merged after dev2 ships here too.

Release explainer, 2026-10-26. Diff v0.4.0.dev2 (3b1a232) to 2823155, the merge of the two integration branches. This is a pre-release. The version bump to 0.4.0.dev3, the changelog section and the releases row come after the diff and are not part of it.

Background

Where these changes came from

0.4.0.dev2 was tagged on 2026-10-21. Two PRs, #12 (test isolation) and #14 (Linux support), reached main after the tag, so they ship here. The rest comes from a review of how cards really ran on a live board, which found problems in four places.

  • Runs lost to the network. A DNS or connection outage counted as a crash, three of them paused all dispatch as systemic, and the pause stayed until the owner ran kanban resume. A run stuck in an endless api_retry loop was never stopped. A 401 or 403 paused the whole account even when the login was fine.
  • CI that proved nothing. A repo with no workflows made wait-ci look like a pass. A worker on a scratch card could open a PR, hit a refusal that said complete, and so skip the warden. A PR could be approved without the Closes line that closes its issue.
  • Review cost. The warden re-ran the full gate even when every check on the head was green and the PR body named that exact sha, and it asked for changes over a screenshot the host could not attach.
  • Multi-card work. Feature branches were a procedure the orchestrator followed by hand. A later part's PR conflicted with a squash-merged earlier one.

The branches were cut from main at 818377e and joined into two integration branches, feature/field-audit-fixes (#16, #17, #18) and feature/milestone-branches (#15). This release is their merge. Line numbers are in the files at the head of this diff.

Walkthrough

Six changes, one at a time

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

Outages and stalls no longer cost a card its retries +added~changed!fixed

What changed
classify() (classify.py:88) has two new verdicts. A run that ends in error with a network message (NETWORK_RE, :8: ENOTFOUND, ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, EAI_AGAIN, ETIMEDOUT, "Can't reach the API server") is network. A run the runner stopped for silence is stalled. Both are in TRANSIENT_OUTCOMES (store.py:222), so they are not counted as failures: end_run sets the retry time to 300 s times 2 to the power of the streak, capped at 1800 s (store.py:2002), which gives 5, 10, 20 and 30 minutes. After six in a row (TRANSIENT_RETRIES, :223), the seventh counts, so a real fault hiding behind "the network" still ends at the failure limit.

The stall watchdog lives in the runner. progress_at (runner.py:581) is reset by each assistant or tool event, judged by is_progress() (classify.py:17): api_retry, status, hook and thinking events say only that claude is alive and do not count. When progress_at + stall_s passes, the runner stops claude and the verdict is stalled (runner.py:605). The new key worker.stall_s defaults to 1200 s (store.py:283); 0 turns the watchdog off, and kanban config set refuses 1 to 699 (store.py:480), because a quiet wait-ci (up to 540 s) or a foreground Bash call (up to 600 s) would be killed as stalled. The clock is not armed while claude waits on background tasks, unless its main thread is retrying the API (stall_armed(), runner.py:621), and it restarts when a background wait or a retry spell begins or ends (:680 to :688).

Two smaller changes. Workers now start with CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0 (runner.py:243), so claude -p waits for background tasks instead of stopping them after 10 minutes. And an auth_lost verdict is confirmed before it pauses the account: login_confirmed_lost() (runner.py:786) runs a fresh login probe, and when the probe passes the outcome becomes network and the account stays open.
Why
An outage is the machine's or the provider's problem, not the card's. Counting it as a crash burned the card's retries, and three of them in ten minutes stopped dispatch for every board. The reverse mistake also existed: a run that sat in api_retry for hours looked alive because those events arrived, so nothing stopped it. The 700 s floor exists only so the watchdog cannot kill a healthy wait.
How you notice it
A card that hit an outage shows network or stalled as the run outcome and starts again after the wait, with no failure counted. kanban config get worker.stall_s prints 1200. The fixtures network_outage.jsonl, stalled.jsonl, background_wait.jsonl and background_wait_outage.jsonl feed the tests in test_classify.py and test_runner.py; test_store.py covers the retry waits and the seventh-run count.

A systemic pause lifts itself +added

What changed
reprobe_dispatch() (dispatcher.py:129) runs from housekeeping (housekeeping.py:293), next to the login probe. It acts only on a pause whose reason is systemic (three crashes in 10 minutes, store.py:217). It asks api_probe() (runner.py:299) for each login a board uses; when none fails, it deletes the pause state and writes a dispatch_resumed event. A failed probe waits longer: 5, 15, then 60 minutes between tries (PROBE_BACKOFF_S, dispatcher.py:18). A pause the owner set, or with any other reason, stays until kanban resume.
Why
A systemic pause used to mean the board stayed idle until the owner noticed, often after an outage that had ended minutes in. The probe is a one-turn Haiku call, so it checks the API and the login without a card's cost.
How you notice it
The event list shows dispatch_paused followed by dispatch_resumed with no owner action. The kanban skill documents both rows (skills/kanban/SKILL.md). test_dispatcher.py adds three cases: the pause lifts when the API answers, a pause changed during the probe is left alone, and an owner pause is never probed away.

CI that proves something, and a PR that cannot skip the warden +added~changed!fixed

What changed
wait-ci. CI_EXIT (worker.py:41) now has two more exit codes. no_ci, exit 6: after a 60 s grace (NO_CI_GRACE_S), _no_ci() (:181) asks the workflows API and the PR head whether the repo has any workflow at all; if it has none, there is nothing to wait for and the answer is never "passed". skipped, exit 7: every check was skipped or neutral (_verdict(), :139), because a pass needs at least one passing check. On a repo that does have workflows, checks that never register make wait-ci stop after 180 s (NO_CHECKS_CAP_S, :40) with the old exit 2. prompts/rules.md no longer says to treat missing CI as passed.

request-review. For a card tied to a GitHub issue, _closes() (worker.py:110) refuses a PR body without Closes OWNER/REPO#N (also Fixes and Resolves, or the issue URL), and says which line to add and the gh pr edit command. agents/smith.md and agents/designer.md list the line in their PR step.

Scratch cards. A scratch card has no repo, so its worker cannot call request-review. Creating, specifying or editing a smith or designer scratch card whose ## Deliverable names a PR is now refused with the worktree flags to use (_dispatchable(), store.py:980). _deliverable_is_pr() (:950) ignores a PR word with a negation in the four words before it in its sentence, so "Do not open a PR" passes. The refusal that a worker meets in request-review (worker.py:75) used to end with "use complete"; it now says to block with needs_input and name the PR.

Preflight. preflight.py prints ok CI green on the head (:87) only when every check on the head passed. A skipped, neutral or unknown bucket now gives a CHECK CI not green line (:79 to :86), and a non-required failing check counts. It reads gh pr checks output when gh exits 1 (failing) or 8 (pending), where it used to report "cannot read the PR".
Why
A skipped job and an absent workflow look like a green PR, and a reviewer who trusts them approves unchecked code. The scratch refusal sent workers the wrong way: following its advice completed the card with a PR that no warden ever saw. The Closes line is what makes GitHub close the issue on merge, and the board's GitHub sync depends on it.
How you notice it
kanban wait-ci on a repo with no workflows exits 6 after about a minute. kanban create ... --assignee smith with a PR deliverable and no --workspace exits 4 with the flags to pass. Tests: test_worker.py covers exits 6 and 7, the 180 s cap, the case where the PR adds the first workflow, and the Closes check; test_store.py covers the create, specify and edit refusals and the negation; test_preflight.py covers the gh exits.

The warden skips a gate re-run that is already proven ~changed

What changed
Section 4 of skills/kanban-code-review/SKILL.md (:37) lets the warden skip its own gate run when two things hold: pre-flight prints ok the Gate line names the head commit (the same sha, not an older ancestor), and every check on the head sha is completed and successful. The Gate: line the builder wrote plus the green checks then stand for the run. A missing, failing, running or absent check keeps the re-run. The approval rule says the same ("gate verified by your run or by the section 4 skip"), and agents/warden.md repeats it in one line.

A second change (:54): where the host cannot attach images to a PR, a written description of what was checked, screenshot files committed under a path in the PR, or file paths named in the PR body all satisfy a screenshot request. The warden no longer requests changes over a missing image alone, unless the card's Deliverable or Acceptance gate requires screenshots and there are none. agents/designer.md (:33) says the same from the builder's side.
Why
A full gate run costs minutes and tokens. When the builder ran it on this sha and CI ran it again and passed, a third run adds cost and no evidence. The screenshot rule removes a review round that could never be satisfied on GitHub Enterprise or in a headless run.
How you notice it
A warden run on a green PR spends fewer turns and its summary names the skip. There is no Python test for skill text; test_surface.py checks only that the files keep their frontmatter.

Milestone branches replace the feature-branch procedure +added~changed

What changed
The kanban skill now decides by itself (skills/kanban/SKILL.md, section "Milestone branches"): two or more smith or designer cards in one repo, or work the owner calls multi-step, become numbered milestones; exactly one code card goes straight to the default branch. A milestone n has a branch milestone/<n>-<slug> that collects its part PRs (merged by the daemon), part branches milestone/<n>-<slug>-<part>, and one finalize card on milestone/<n>-<slug>-final. references/feature-branch.md is gone; references/milestone-branches.md replaces it.

The finalize card's branch is always cut from the default branch and given --base <default>, so its PR cannot go to the milestone branch by accident. It replays only milestone n's own commits with git cherry-pick over git rev-list --topo-order --reverse --no-merges origin/<prev>..origin/milestone/<n>-<slug>. When the warden approves, the card is done and the board shows awaiting_owner_merge; the orchestrator tells the owner, then starts milestone n+1's parts while n waits. Milestone n+1's finalize card is created only after gh pr view reports MERGED for n.

The runtime change is small. protection.py:57 now samples a milestone/* branch as well as the default and a feature/* branch for doctor check 19, and the README's branch-protection ruleset covers both patterns. cli.md says --merge-method is for the daemon's merge into a milestone or feature branch.
Why
After the owner squash-merges milestone 1, the default branch holds copies of its commits, while milestone 2, cut from milestone 1, still holds the originals. Merging the default into milestone 2 conflicts wherever both touched a line, whichever merge command the owner used, and a worker cannot force-push a rewritten branch. Replaying only milestone 2's own commits onto the fresh default branch avoids both problems. It replaced the single feature branch because that branch was one long-lived line: the owner could merge nothing until the whole piece of work was done, and the next stage had to wait for that one big PR. The owner asked for long-term work to arrive as a series of milestone PRs, each merged when convenient, with the agent carrying on with the next milestone meanwhile; numbered milestones with their own finalize PR give exactly that.
How you notice it
Ask the orchestrator for work in several parts: it creates the milestone branch and the part cards without asking. test_milestone.py builds real git repos: test_m1 merges milestone 1 by squash, merge and rebase and checks that milestone 2's replay is a clean PR each time; test_m3 checks that a child of an approved finalize card starts at approval, not at the owner's merge, which is why the finalize cards cannot be chained; test_m4 runs the reference's exact commands.

Already on main: Linux, and tests independent of the environment +added!fixed~changed

What changed
PR #14 (Linux). systemd.py writes the unit ~/.config/systemd/user/kanban-claude.daemon.service (mode 0600, Restart=on-failure, KillMode=process so a daemon restart leaves detached runners alone) and drives it with systemctl --user. service.py picks the backend by platform, and the environment scrub that launchd.py held moved there. Setup needs systemctl on Linux, says to pass --no-daemon when it is missing, and warns with loginctl enable-linger when lingering is off. Doctor checks 1, 12, 13 and 17 name the LaunchAgent or the unit by platform.

Two fixes in procs.py. start_time() ran ps in the C locale but parsed the date in the daemon's own locale, so with LC_TIME=de_DE.UTF-8 and no LANG every worker crashed at claim. On Linux it now reads /proc/<pid>/stat and the boot time from /proc/stat; on macOS it reads the English date by hand. boot_time() returned 0 on Linux (sysctl kern.boottime is macOS only), so a run left running by a reboot was never reclaimed.

PR #12. Two tests no longer depend on the environment the runner is started in.
Why
These were merged to main after the 0.4.0.dev2 tag and have not been in a release. The CHANGELOG already listed them under 0.4.0.dev2; they move to the 0.4.0.dev3 section.
How you notice it
On Linux, /kanban-claude:setup installs and starts the unit; kanban doctor check 1 names it. test_systemd.py (201 lines) and test_procs.py cover the unit text and the /proc parsing.

Known limits

What this release does not do

  • A crash loop the API probe passes. If every run crashes for a reason the one-turn probe cannot see, such as a broken plugin, the systemic pause lifts after about 5 minutes and trips again after three more crashes. The probe checks the API and the login, not whether a worker starts.
  • A 403 on one model. If a model returns 403 while the Haiku probe passes, the verdict becomes network, is retried six times and then counted. It is not reported as an auth problem.
  • Milestone ordering is the orchestrator's habit, not a board rule. Milestone n+1's finalize card waits for gh pr view ... state == MERGED only because the skill says so; the board does not check it.
  • The scratch negation check reads only the words before the PR word. "Do not open a PR" passes; a negation written after it ("a PR is not wanted") does not (store.py:951).
  • A background task that hangs for good is left to the runtime cap, because the watchdog is not armed while claude waits on one (runner.py:621).

Upgrade notes

Moving from 0.4.0.dev2 to 0.4.0.dev3

  1. Run /kanban-claude:setup between cards so the daemon and the CLI move together. The schema stays at 7: no migration, no backup. The daemon restart does not touch runs in flight, but a run that began under 0.4.0.dev2 has no stall watchdog.
  2. Run kanban doctor. Check 19 now also reads protection on one milestone/* branch per repo. To cover both patterns, use the ruleset in the README's "Branch protection" section (refs/heads/feature/* and refs/heads/milestone/*, no pull-request rule, forbid delete and non-fast-forward).
  3. On Linux, set up needs systemctl --user, and loginctl enable-linger $USER once, or the daemon stops when your last session ends.
  4. On a repo with no workflows, wait-ci now exits 6, and the worker writes "no CI on this repo" in its summary and on the PR's Gate: line instead of reporting a pass. The warden sees that wording; decide per repo whether a check should exist.
  5. A scratch smith or designer card whose body asks for a PR can no longer be created or edited; recreate it with --workspace worktree:<repo> --branch <branch>. Cards that already exist are not changed.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Six questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. A DNS outage ends a run. What does the board do with the card?

network is in TRANSIENT_OUTCOMES, so the retry time is 300 s doubled per earlier run in the streak, capped at 1800 s. The seventh in a row counts, so a hidden real fault still ends at the failure limit.

2. You run kanban config set worker.stall_s 300. What happens?

wait-ci can be quiet for 540 s and a foreground Bash call for 600 s, so a shorter watchdog would kill a healthy wait (store.py:480). 0 turns the watchdog off.

3. A repo has no workflows. A smith runs kanban wait-ci. What does it get?

After NO_CI_GRACE_S the verb asks the workflows API and the PR head; with no workflow on either, nothing will ever report, and the answer is never a pass. Exit 7 is the separate case where checks exist and all were skipped.

4. The warden may skip its own gate run. Which pair of facts is needed?

A running or missing check keeps the re-run, and so does a Gate: line that names an older ancestor of the head.

5. Milestone 1 was squash-merged. Why does milestone 2's finalize card replay commits instead of merging the default branch into milestone 2?

The replay applies only milestone 2's own commits to a fresh branch cut from the default, so the PR is clean whichever way the owner merged milestone 1 (test_m1 checks squash, merge and rebase).

6. Which of these is a known limit of this release?

The probe checks the API and the login, not that a worker starts, so a broken plugin looks healthy to it. The pause trips again after three more crashes.
